shut up!` and references with exactly the source before one history append. A non-Hidden matching target instead gets a separate immediate retained history entry. There is no unsubscribe, source-liveness check, or one-shot guard; multiple matching callbacks overwrite in combine order and the last writer wins.

An ordinary allowed click changes the character from Hidden to Alive before the state callback reaches RevealCard, which calls Day before OnReveal. Role.OnActed therefore invokes the registered delegate on the non-Hidden card; both Rambler truth paths uniformly choose from the same 34 flavor quotes and emit exact predecessor/successor references, including small-board duplicates. The quote is constraint-free. maxTimesPicked is initialized to one but neither times-picked field is read or written by any other Rambler2 method.

The shipped public Good Outcast Bombardier CharacterData binds exact managed Saint, is bluffable but non-picking, owns no serialized statuses or achievement, and authors the narrow text 'Lose if you Execute me.' A separate shipped Villager named Saint embeds managed SaintVillager and is not this binding.

Managed Saint supplies the broader description 'Lose if you Kill me', fresh empty real and bluff ActedInfo records, an all-trigger no-op Act, and a base-only constructor. Inherited bluff dispatch reaches that same no-op, while base killability and wrong-execution damage remain true and five; the role owns no picker, result, local state, reset, or achievement logic.

Ordinary execution, ExecuteAndReveal, KillAndReveal/Slayer, and Character.Kill can publish successful non-Demon deaths to the dead list and terminal checker; the forced routes bypass ordinary killability. A successful delayed Demon kill instead sets killedByDemon before death publication, while a rejected or already-dead target does not complete that path.

The highest-precedence automatic-loss predicate requires a dead entry with killedByDemon false and follows that entry's current Character.dataRef to its exact managed Saint role type. It does not use stable/original physical identity, the cloned role, bluff/display, register-as data, alignment, or status. Genuine dataRef replacement to Bombardier is therefore fatal even with preserved Evil alignment, while ordinary bluff and Drunk/Doppel display copies are not; exact SaintVillager also does not match.
